evidence.claim: Article 104 vests executive authority in the President, including national-security policy, treaty ratification, appointment and dismissal of ministers and senior officials, military-use decisions, and presidential decrees subject to legal limits; Article 116 lets the TBMM or the President renew elections; Article 105 sets a parliamentary investigation path.
evidence.title: Anayasa | Anayasa Mahkemesi
evidence.excerpt: Article 104 vests executive authority in the President, including national-security policy, treaty ratification, appointment and dismissal of ministers and senior officials, military-use decisions, and presidential decrees subject to legal limits; Article 116 lets the TBMM or the President renew elections; Article 105 sets a parliamentary investigation path.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary constitutional text governing the 2022 presidency; direct and stable legal authority/constraint source.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Defines Erdoğan's office-level authority and checks in 2022; not a claim about personal conduct.
contrary_evidence: The same articles constrain decree power and preserve parliamentary/judicial checks.
Formal authority does not prove how he used it in practice.

evidence.claim: The evaluation found the program was an extension of the national CCTE launched in 2017, built on the Ministry of Family, Labour and Social Services' 2003 program for vulnerable families, and its child-protection component operated in 15 provinces.
evidence.title: Programme Evaluation of the Conditional Cash Transfer for Education (CCTE) for Syrians and Other Refugees in Turkey
evidence.excerpt: The evaluation found the program was an extension of the national CCTE launched in 2017, built on the Ministry of Family, Labour and Social Services' 2003 program for vulnerable families, and its child-protection component operated in 15 provinces.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent mixed-methods evaluation with clear program history and institutional design detail.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective but directly informative about the 2022 welfare architecture and durability.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partial: the program predated 2022, but it reflects state social-policy architecture maintained under Erdoğan.
contrary_evidence: The report notes the program was donor-supported and its child-protection arm had limited resources.

evidence.claim: The government introduced measures to shield vulnerable groups from rising energy and food prices, the number of households receiving energy assistance doubled to 4 million, and electricity tariffs for low-consumption households were cut.
evidence.title: Türkiye: OECD Economic Outlook, Volume 2022 Issue 2
evidence.excerpt: The government introduced measures to shield vulnerable groups from rising energy and food prices, the number of households receiving energy assistance doubled to 4 million, and electricity tariffs for low-consumption households were cut.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: OECD surveillance note gives a concrete policy measure with quantified coverage and direct distributional framing.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partial: this was Erdoğan-era policy, though the need arose from the inflation shock and energy-price environment.
contrary_evidence: The same OECD chapter warns that households in the lowest decile spend nearly 70% of their budget on food and housing, and inflation remained above 40%.

evidence.claim: When HDI is adjusted for inequality, Türkiye's ranking falls to 63rd of 166 countries, and men enjoy a higher level of human development than women.
evidence.title: Türkiye ranks 45th of 193 countries in human development, new UNDP report says
evidence.excerpt: When HDI is adjusted for inequality, Türkiye's ranking falls to 63rd of 166 countries, and men enjoy a higher level of human development than women.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Same UNDP release includes a clear inequality-adjusted comparison and gender gap warning.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective on 2022 data; directly relevant to distribution and dignity.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partial: this reflects structural inequality under the Erdoğan-era state, but not all of it is uniquely attributable to 2022 decisions.
contrary_evidence: The same release also emphasizes strong overall HDI progress over the long run.

evidence.claim: The 2022 Istanbul meeting brought together governments, partner agencies, and civil society to set priorities for refugee and migrant health, and the outcome statement unanimously endorsed five pillars of action to make health a reality for all.
evidence.title: Report on the High-level Meeting on Health and Migration: 17–18 March 2022, Istanbul
evidence.excerpt: The 2022 Istanbul meeting brought together governments, partner agencies, and civil society to set priorities for refugee and migrant health, and the outcome statement unanimously endorsed five pillars of action to make health a reality for all.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: WHO technical document is a solid record of a policy forum, though it is more about coordination than direct delivery.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partial/contextual: it reflects government-hosted coordination rather than a single ruler-specific welfare act.
contrary_evidence: A meeting is not the same as implementation, so this is weaker than the delivery evidence above.

evidence.claim: UNICEF says Türkiye has vulnerable children including refugees, children with disabilities, and children living in poverty, and that it works with the government on literacy, numeracy, special education, counselling services, and communication support for Syrian families.
evidence.title: Systems-strengthening, inclusive basic education and learning
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF says Türkiye has vulnerable children including refugees, children with disabilities, and children living in poverty, and that it works with the government on literacy, numeracy, special education, counselling services, and communication support for Syrian families.
evidence.source_locator: page text shown in search snippet and page body summary
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UNICEF program page is directly relevant to inclusion and service design, but it is a general program description rather than a dated audit.
evidence.period_fit: Program context relevant to 2022 welfare institutions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partial/contextual: it describes an ongoing government-UNICEF partnership inside the Turkish system.
contrary_evidence: The page does not by itself show 2022 delivery or outcomes.

evidence.claim: UNICEF says Türkiye still has one of the lowest net pre-primary enrolment rates among OECD countries and that it prioritizes accessible, inclusive, good-quality early learning for the most vulnerable children while working with the Ministry of National Education to expand good-quality spaces.
evidence.title: Early Childhood Education
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF says Türkiye still has one of the lowest net pre-primary enrolment rates among OECD countries and that it prioritizes accessible, inclusive, good-quality early learning for the most vulnerable children while working with the Ministry of National Education to expand good-quality spaces.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UNICEF program page is clear on priorities and the baseline challenge, but it is not a year-specific evaluation.
evidence.period_fit: Context for 2022 social-policy conditions and durable institutional goals.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partial/contextual: the page reflects ongoing ministry-UNICEF cooperation, not a single 2022 decision.
contrary_evidence: It says the challenge is persistent, which limits claims of decisive 2022 success.

unresolved_gaps: Direct 2022 nuclear-specific conduct is sparse; most positive evidence is alliance or humanitarian diplomacy rather than nuclear command, doctrine, or safety reform.
The package shows limited exposure and inherited NATO structure, but not a strong ruler-attributed improvement or deterioration in nuclear posture.

The package is strong on mediation and selective coercion, but weaker on independent verification of the civilian-harm allegations and on Erdoğan's own weighing of peaceful alternatives for the Syria/Iraq operations.
Several items are civic-space or press-repression evidence rather than direct physical-integrity harm, so the chapter partly relies on fear-climate inference.
Attribution for some harms is institutional rather than command-specific, especially for local policing and court actions.
There was no true 2022 succession or term-limit stress test, so the chapter relies on institutional erosion and media/election-law evidence instead of a direct transfer-of-power event.
Outcomes are heavily confounded by inflation shocks, external demand, the post-pandemic rebound, and CBRT formal independence, so causal credit remains partial.
Project-level delivery and regional/household distribution evidence are thinner than macro indicators.
The strongest welfare evidence is on health coverage and refugee cash transfers; housing, sanitation, and school-quality evidence is thinner.
Several positive items are donor-UNICEF/WHO partnerships, so Erdoğan attribution is meaningful but not exclusive.
There is no direct 2022 audited asset, gift, or procurement record for Erdoğan personally.
The strongest negative items are media-control and family-network allegations, not direct first-person dishonesty or self-dealing proof.
Project-level completion evidence is thin; the package shows allocation, program design, and some outcomes, but not audited delivery for specific 2022 initiatives.
Outcome attribution is still confounded by shocks and by private-sector behavior, especially on growth, exports, and labor-market statistics.
